Management System Certification Body Public Statement

Document No. MSCB-A-02 | Version 261106A | Release date 2026-11-06

← Public Documents

1. Scope

1.1 This statement sets out the body's public commitments, as a management system certification body, regarding impartiality, confidentiality, public information, certification status, use of certificates and marks, and the handling of appeals and complaints.

1.2 This statement applies to information disclosed publicly by the body concerning its management system certification activities, including AIMS, ISMS, PIMS, CMS, RSMS and other management system certification schemes approved by the body.

2. Normative References

2.1 This statement refers to the requirements of ISO/IEC 17021-1:2015 concerning principles, general requirements, information requirements, and the handling of appeals and complaints.

Note: The corresponding National Standard of the Republic of China is CNS 17021-1:2019, Conformity assessment — Requirements for bodies providing audit and certification of management systems — Part 1: Requirements.

3. Terms and Definitions

3.1 This statement uses terms commonly applied in management system certification. Questions concerning terminology, certification services or the application of this statement may be directed to the body.

4. Statement on Impartiality

4.1 The body is committed to having management system certification activities conducted impartially, objectively and independently by competent personnel, and is responsible for the certification decisions it makes.

4.2 The body, any part of the same legal entity and any entity under the organizational control of the body shall not offer or provide to applicant organizations or certified clients (including ISO/IEC 42001 certification clients) consultancy on management systems, artificial intelligence, information security, privacy, data protection (e.g. in the form of an external data protection officer or data protection check) or risk management, nor offer, provide or assist in performing internal audits or internal reviews of the management system of an applicant organization or certified client. The body shall not link, bundle or confuse certification activities with consultancy activities, circumvent the prohibition on internal audits by describing the activity as an inspection, assessment, review or otherwise, or imply that using specified consultants, training or services would result in a more favourable certification outcome.

Note: The content of this subclause relates to ISO/IEC 17021-1, subclause 5.2.5; ISO/IEC 27706, subclause 5.2.2; ISO/IEC 42006, subclause 5.2.2.1.

4.3 The body identifies, evaluates and treats risks that may affect impartiality, including those arising from ownership, governance, management, finances, business relationships, external personnel, client relationships and other conflicts of interest.

4.4 The body oversees risks to impartiality through the Impartiality Committee. Any person who becomes aware of circumstances that may affect the impartiality of the body's certification activities may submit information or a complaint to the body.

5. Statement on Confidentiality

5.1 The body is responsible for maintaining the confidentiality of client information, personal data, technical data, information security data, privacy information, artificial intelligence system information, compliance incidents and other confidential information obtained during certification activities.

5.2 Except as required by law or for information obtained by the accreditation body under accreditation requirements, the body does not disclose confidential client information without the written consent of the client. When disclosure is required by law or by a regulatory authority, the body will notify the client unless prohibited by law.

6. Certification Information and Certification Status

6.1 The body provides management system certification for:

  1. Artificial intelligence management systems (AIMS, ISO/IEC 42001).
  2. Information security management systems (ISMS, ISO/IEC 27001).
  3. Privacy information management systems (PIMS, ISO/IEC 27701).
  4. Compliance management systems (CMS, ISO 37301).
  5. Service robot safety management systems (RSMS, ISO 31101).

The body also makes the following publicly available on its website at https://aisml.org:

  1. Its certification requirements.
  2. Application methods.
  3. Processes for handling appeals and complaints.
  4. Requirements for the use of certificates and marks.

6.2 Any person may request, and the body will provide, the following information: the geographical areas in which the body operates; the status of a given certification; and the name, related normative document, scope and geographical location (city and country) of a specific certified client. In exceptional cases, access to certain information may be limited at the request of the certified client, for example for security reasons.

6.3 A management system certification certificate issued by the body indicates only that the certified client's management system, within the scope stated on the certificate, conforms to the applicable certification criteria. It does not constitute a product conformity assurance by the body for the certified client's products, services, process outputs or individual activities.

6.4 The body's audit and certification process is as follows:

  1. After the applicant organization submits an application, the body completes the application review and concludes the certification agreement, and then conducts stage 1 and stage 2 of the initial certification audit.
  2. The certification decision is made by a Certification Decision-Maker who did not participate in the audit.
  3. The certification cycle is three years.
  4. Except in the year of recertification, at least one surveillance audit is conducted in each calendar year; the first surveillance audit following initial certification is conducted no later than 12 months from the date of the certification decision.
  5. A recertification audit is conducted before expiry.
  6. On the basis of audit results and other information, the body decides to grant, refuse, maintain, renew, suspend, restore or withdraw certification, or to expand or reduce the scope of certification.
  7. The body conducts special audits where necessary.

6.5 Requests for information about the body's certification services, certification status or the content of this statement may be submitted by email (Service@aisml.org). The body will acknowledge receipt and reply within 14 working days.

7. Use of Certificates and Marks

7.1 Certified clients shall use certificates, marks and references to certification in accordance with the body's rules and applicable accreditation requirements and shall not imply, in a misleading manner, that any scope, product, service or site not covered has been certified.

7.2 If the body identifies misuse of a certificate, mark or reference to certification, it may require the certified client to correct the misuse, discontinue use, issue a public correction, suspend or withdraw certification, or take other necessary action in accordance with applicable requirements.

8. Appeals and Complaints

8.1 Any applicant organization, client or certified client that disagrees with a certification decision made by the body in relation to that party may lodge an appeal with the body.

8.2 Any person or organization dissatisfied with the body's certification activities, the management system of a certified client, the use of certificates or marks, impartiality, confidentiality or service quality may lodge a complaint with the body.

8.3 The body will handle appeals and complaints in an impartial, confidential and traceable manner. Personnel participating in the appeal process will be different from those who carried out the original audit and made the original certification decision. A decision communicated to an appellant or complainant will be made by, or reviewed and approved by, personnel who were not previously involved in the appeal or the subject of the complaint.

8.4 Appeals and Complaints Email: Service@aisml.org

8.5 The process for handling appeals and complaints is summarized as follows:

  1. The appeal or complaint is received, and its receipt is acknowledged to the person who submitted it within 5 working days of receipt.
  2. The appeal or complaint is validated and investigated; the investigation of an appeal takes into account the results of previous similar appeals.
  3. The actions needed are determined and a decision is made; the decision is made by, or reviewed and approved by, personnel not previously involved in the case.
  4. The person who submitted the appeal or complaint is informed of the outcome.
  5. The handling is tracked and recorded, and appropriate correction and corrective actions are taken in accordance with MSCB-B-13.

9. Maintenance of this Statement

9.1 The body will maintain this statement so that it remains consistent with the certification services actually provided and applicable requirements. The body will evaluate and update this statement as appropriate when its certification services, public information, appeal and complaint processes, rules for the use of certificates and marks, or applicable requirements change.
